title: Perennial ryegrass fraction composition and nitrogen recovery by spring cutting date
citation: Stødkilde, L., Eriksen, J., & Jensen, S.K. (2020). Biorefined grasses and legumes – effect of species and spring cutting date on extractable protein yield. Grassland Science in Europe, 25, proceedings paper, pp. 683–684.
source_location: Proceedings PDF pp. 683–684; Tables 1, 2 and 3; methods on p. 683.
license: No explicit reuse license identified in the proceedings PDF; source data are transcribed with attribution and retained as reference-only.
material_scope: Cultivated perennial ryegrass (Lolium perenne) harvested on four consecutive spring dates in a replicated plot study; samples were frozen before laboratory screw pressing.
process_conditions: Pulp and green juice were produced with an Angel 8500s laboratory screw press. Soluble proteins were precipitated by adding 12 M phosphoric acid to pH 4; acidified juice was held overnight at 4 C before fraction analysis.
data_scope: Twenty values transcribed from Tables 1–3: herbage nitrogen concentration, pulp and protein-isolate nitrogen concentrations, and source-calculated nitrogen recovery to pulp and protein isolate for perennial ryegrass only.
limitations: Cultivated ryegrass is an analogue, not roadside grass or the GreenHub VARTA feedstock.

Recovery is total nitrogen partitioning computed from sample mass balances and N analyses, not isolated true-protein recovery; the source reports that some calculated fraction recoveries can exceed 100% due to sample-level mass-balance variation.
The paper reports group SEM and significance tests, not date-specific uncertainty for each ryegrass observation; no replicate-level values were inferred.
The source reports acid concentration and target pH but not the acid volume or acid equivalents consumed; this does not close GreenHub's titration/reagent-demand gap.
All observations are reference-only and do not activate GreenHub defaults or equations.
conversion_method: No numeric conversions applied; source values, units, basis, dates, and table locations are retained as reported.
uncertainty: Date-specific uncertainties are not reported for the ryegrass rows in the tables; pooled SEM values are not assigned to individual dates.
